text:
Emma (support): Hey @Acme Integration — picking up your support ticket about the batch rerank mismatch. Can you paste the exact request body and the raw response you saw? Even a trimmed sample for 2 queries would help.

Acme Integration: quick dump below. We send two queries in one batch with different candidate sets. Response scores map to the wrong queries (seems shifted). Using v1/rerank endpoint.

Acme Integration: ```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "model": "redwood-rerank-1",
  "queries": ["who wrote gulag archipelago", "best italian restaurants sf"],
  "candidates": [
    ["alexander solzhenitsyn", "soviet author", "gulag history"],
    ["trattoria roma", "pizza place north beach"]
  ],
  "batching": { "mode": "per_query_list" }
}
```

Acme Integration: Response (trimmed):
```json
{
  "scores": [0.92, 0.81, 0.79, 0.44, 0.38],
  "candidates_flat": ["alexander solzhenitsyn", "trattoria roma", "soviet author", "pizza place north beach", "gulag history"]
}
```

Acme Integration: The problem: scores are not aligned with their original per-query candidate group. We expected 3 scores for query1 then 2 for query2 but the flattening order is different. This started after we upgraded to SDK 0.9.5.

Emma (support): Thanks — that helps. Two immediate asks: (1) can you confirm the HTTP response headers (content-type, x-request-id, x-redwood-version)? (2) can you try the same request with the raw curl (no SDK) so we can rule out client-side transform?

Acme Integration: headers: `x-request-id: r-abc123`, `x-redwood-version: v2026-03-05`, `content-type: application/json`. I ran raw curl and got the same misorder. Curl below: ```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-rerank-1","queries":["q1","q2"],"candidates":[["a","b","c"],["d","e"]]}'
```

Raj (eng-runtime): Assigning to me. Quick hypothesis: we changed the internal flatten order in the last release to optimize memory layout; it now flattens by candidate insertion time rather than by query index when candidates arrays contain unequal lengths and some elements are identical strings. That could lead to perceived "phase shift". Can you share the full raw request payload you send to the server (including empty strings or nulls)? Sometimes trailing empty arrays get coalesced.

Acme Integration: Full payload attached in ticket. Nothing exotic, no nulls. I can repro reliably: create queries lengths [3,2] with candidate strings unique and results come back in [1,4,2,5,3] order (mapped by positions).

Raj (eng-runtime): Repro steps I ran locally: used your payload and hit the local stub of rerank runtime. I saw the same pattern. Debug logs show the flattening routine computing offsets as [0,1,3] (which is wrong for 3,2) because we accidentally used prefix sums over sorted(candidate_hash) rather than per-query prefix sums. Oops.

Raj (eng-runtime): Minimal repro I used: ```python
queries = ["qA","qB"]
candidates = [["A1","A2","A3"],["B1","B2"]]
# expected offsets: [0,3,5]
# bad offsets (current): [0,1,3]
```

Mari (product): How urgent is this for Acme? Do they have production traffic affected or is it a dev testing issue?

Acme Integration: This broke our site search ranking A/B test today — production impact, ~15% of rerank calls use batching like this. We rolled back SDK initially but saw same from curl, so it's server-side.

Emma (support): Escalating to severity-high. Notifying oncall and scheduling a quick rollback for the flattening change. Raj, can you confirm whether a hotfix is trivial (replacing the prefix-sum code path) and whether we need to invalidate caches / model instances?

Raj (eng-runtime): Hotfix plan: revert the memory-order optimization for per_query_list mode and add unit tests for varied-length lists. I will push a patch to release branch and roll through canary 1% -> 25% -> 100% if checks pass. No cache invalidation required because this is deterministic flattening change, not model state.

deploy-bot: deploy started by raj. Patch: rerank/flatten_fix. Canary 1% -> 2 nodes.

Emma (support): Acme — we'll monitor. In the meantime, workaround: send single-query batches or avoid mixed-length candidate lists if urgent. Also we'll provide a signed timeline for customers.

Raj (eng-runtime): Canary showed correct offsets on node A, but node B still returned old behavior due to an old binary not fully evicted from the autoscaler. Forcing restart on that node now.

deploy-bot: node B drained and restarted. Canary metrics: error rate 0, alignment tests OK. Rolling to 25%.

Acme Integration: Confirmed — our test requests now return candidates in the correct per-query order. Scores look aligned. Thank you.

Emma (support): Closing the loop: cause = change in flattening order introduced to optimize memory layout; symptom = per-query candidate lists misordered when candidate counts vary and some candidate strings collide/hash in a particular way; fix = revert to stable per-query prefix sum flattening + unit tests + stricter integration test in CI.

Mari (product): Action items: (1) release notes entry referencing rerank fix and recommended temporary workarounds, (2) customer comms for impacted customers (Acme + others flagged by alert), (3) postmortem to track why the optimization landed without integration tests.

Emma (support): I'll draft the customer note and ping @acme_integration with ETA. Raj — please add the revert PR and link the CI test in this thread.

Raj (eng-runtime): PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/rerank/+/1234 — includes unit tests and a small integration harness. Will follow up with perf numbers; expect <1% memory regression but correctness fixed.

Acme Integration: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Can you include an assertion we can run client-side to detect misalignment automatically? We can gate on that in our deploys.

Raj (eng-runtime): Good idea — I'll add a response sanity flag : `per_query_alignment_check: true` that returns an array of per-query counts in the response when enabled (dev-only for now).

Emma (support): Thanks everyone — marking this thread resolved for support. Follow-up items tracked in ticket #SUP-9876 and PR notes. :white_check_mark:
